name: matchpairs
expr: [M1, uR1, uC1] = matchpairs(C1, 100); t1 = 0; for k = 1:size(M1,1); t1 = t1 + C1(M1(k,1), M1(k,2)); end; [M2, uR2, uC2] = matchpairs(C2, 20); t2 = 0; for k = 1:size(M2,1); t2 = t2 + C2(M2(k,1), M2(k,2)); end; [M3, uR3, uC3] = matchpairs(C3, 100); t3 = 0; for k = 1:size(M3,1); t3 = t3 + C3(M3(k,1), M3(k,2)); end; [Mmx, ~, ~] = matchpairs(Cmax, 0, 'max'); tmx = 0; for k = 1:size(Mmx,1); tmx = tmx + Cmax(Mmx(k,1), Mmx(k,2)); end;
comment: Sig: [M, uR, uC] = matchpairs(Cost, costUnmatched [, 'min'|'max']) — linear assignment / bipartite matching on rectangular Cost. 'min' (default): minimise total cost with costUnmatched as the per-row/col unmatched penalty. 'max': maximise total benefit with costUnmatched as the per-row/col REWARD for leaving unmatched (note: a high positive costUnmatched in 'max' mode leaves everything unmatched — matches MATLAB R2025b's documented convention). Algorithm: Jonker-Volgenant Hungarian on the augmented (m+n)×(m+n) matrix; 'max' negates both Cost and costUnmatched before solving. Total cost is what we fingerprint — assignment ordering is engine-dependent, totals are unique. Bit-exact MATLAB R2025b (tol=0) on the documented test cases.
